exposure: proportion of cervical volume/length excised during CIN treatment
cohort: The study included 142 women undergoing cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) treatment at a university hospital between 2009 and 2013.
finding: The pregnancy duration at delivery was significantly and negatively correlated with the proportion of the cervical volume and length excised, and the cone volume, indicating that a larger excision correlates with a shorter pregnancy duration.
